flows.title: Synced Lua immediate destruction to ID reuse

steps.description: Parses the unit and cleanupImmediately argument, bounds recursive DestroyUnit calls, and invokes ForcedKillUnit.
Marks the unit dead, releases transportees, invokes destruction callbacks, removes wind registration, and marks reclaimed or unfinished units ready for deletion.
After ForcedKillUnit returns, requests immediate garbage collection when cleanupImmediately was supplied.
Refuses during UnitHandler update scopes; otherwise queues and deletes the unit, then recycles the ID.
Removes team and active-unit references, frees the ID, clears the units slot, frees the object, and destroys its entity.

flows.title: Factory cancellation refund and death bookkeeping

steps.description: A factory stop command calls the factory StopBuild routine before consuming the command.
Stops the build script; for an unfinished product, returns invested metal and kills it as reclaimed before dropping the build dependence and pointers.
Runs transport, destruction callback, wind, and death-script bookkeeping for the canceled product.

flows.title: Lua command description removal to queue pruning

steps.description: Requires FullCtrl, resolves a one-based optional command-description index, and calls RemoveCommandDescription.
Bounds-checks the index and routes the removed command ID through HandleBuildOptionRemoval before erasing the description.
For a negative build command, removes every matching queued builder or factory command and erases the build option.
Stops a factory build when the active product no longer matches the build-queue front.

flows.title: Mutable unit costs to cancellation and reclaim arithmetic

steps.description: Accepts numeric Lua values and assigns build time, metal cost, or energy cost after only a lower-bound std::max expression.
Computes a cancellation metal return from the mutable metal cost and build progress.
Uses mutable cost values for build consumption and reclaim refund calculations, then kills a fully reclaimed unit.

facts.statement: DestroyUnit calls ForcedKillUnit before it requests immediate garbage collection; ForcedKillUnit releases transportees and emits UnitDestroyed callbacks before removing wind registration and setting deathScriptFinished.

The cleanupImmediately argument is documented as unconditional removal and immediate ID reuse, but GarbageCollectUnit returns false during UnitHandler update scopes and the Lua caller does not inspect that result.
Successful immediate collection removes the unit from team and active indices, frees its ID, clears the units slot, frees the object, and destroys the entity before RecycleID returns.
UnitHandler marks inUpdateCall around pre-frame updates, the main unit update pipeline, and post-animation transport updates; GarbageCollectUnit refuses immediate deletion throughout those regions.
ForcedKillUnit marks the unit dead, resolves transported units, emits destruction callbacks, unregisters wind generators, and makes reclaimed or unfinished units eligible for deletion.
Wind bookkeeping stores unit IDs and later dereferences GetUnit(id) without a local null check, so removing a generator ID before physical deletion or ID reuse is a required ordering invariant.
Factory StopBuild returns metal equal to current product metal cost times build progress, kills the unfinished product as reclaimed, removes the build death dependence, and clears product pointers.
Negative AddBuildPower computes energy and metal reclaim terms from mutable unit costs, issues a resource order, and kills the unit as reclaimed when progress or health reaches zero.
SetUnitCosts checks Lua number type and applies a lower-bound std::max, but contains no explicit finite-value predicate before assigning buildTime, metal cost, or energy cost.

A positive-infinite Lua number can plausibly survive the lower-bound expression and then enter factory cancellation or reclaim arithmetic. This is a source-based hypothesis that requires a controlled finite-value regression; this chapter does not establish a reproduced engine failure.
RemoveUnitCmdDesc routes a removed negative command ID through HandleBuildOptionRemoval, which removes every matching command from builder or factory queues and erases the corresponding build option.

Any atomic factory replacement path should distinguish callback execution from physical deletion, prove that old IDs and pointers cannot be reused while callbacks still observe them, preserve wind/transport/death-dependence cleanup, reject nonfinite mutable costs, and verify build-option removal against the active factory product and queue. These are derived test obligations, not proof of a defect in Recoil 7555.

A separate unprotected FR2 lifetime candidate was reported at local source identifier d9690a37b72489ff6749229b589762b5c3a9f86f, branch routine/barc-fr2-lifetime-reentrancy-20260930. It is not registered as current or protected source, and native acceptance remains reported as 0/6.

open_questions: Which callback or nested Lua route, if any, attempts cleanupImmediately while a factory replacement transaction still holds raw unit or command pointers?
Should cleanupImmediately report a refused immediate collection when UnitHandler is inside an update scope instead of silently retaining deferred cleanup semantics?
Do Lua numeric conversion and every supported platform preserve positive infinity through SetUnitCosts, and which explicit finite-value policy should apply?
Can removing a build option race or reenter with factory StopBuild such that the active product, queue front, death dependence, or refund basis diverges?
Which controlled tests distinguish safe callback completion, wind and transport cleanup, ID reuse, refund conservation, and command queue consistency for a future atomic replacement implementation?
